channel.title: Honolulu Star-Advertiser
channel.description: Hawaii News, Sports, Weather and Entertainment

item.title: Holei Sea Arch has collapsed
item.dc:creator: Star-Advertiser Staff
item.description: The Holei Sea Arch has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean, federal officials confirmed.

item.title: Lifeguards revive pulse in man pulled from Hanauma Bay
item.dc:creator: Star-Advertiser Staff
item.description: Honolulu Ocean Safety lifeguards rescued an older man who became unresponsive while swimming at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve this morning.

item.title: DOH closes Legend at Chinatown Cultural Plaza for multiple violations
item.dc:creator: Star-Advertiser Staff
item.description: The state Health Department today shut down Legend Seafood Restaurant at Chinatown Cultural Plaza, with a red placard, due to multiple critical food safety violations.

item.title: SpaceX launches 13th long-duration astronaut crew to International Space Station
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: CAPE CANAVERAL, Florida >> A SpaceX rocket lifted off from Florida on Thursday with a crew of two U.S. astronauts, a Canadian astronaut and a Russian cosmonaut headed to the International Space Station for a science mission devoted to human health and performance in orbit.

item.title: Massachusetts man indicted for alleged cyberstalking Stephen Miller’s wife
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: BOSTON >> Federal prosecutors on Thursday charged a Massachusetts man with cyberstalking the wife of White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, accusing him of repeatedly calling and texting her and sending vulgar messages to her and her parents.

item.title: Wall Street dips as rising Treasury yields outweigh software gains
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: The S&P 500 fell to a two-week low on Thursday as a global bond selloff, fueled by higher oil prices and inflation concerns, pushed US Treasury yields to multi-decade highs and overshadowed a rally in software stocks.

item.title: McCormick’s price hikes spice up quarterly results despite sluggish demand
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: McCormick reported higher quarterly sales and profit on Thursday, as pricier seasonings and sauces helped cushion the blow from weaker consumer demand due to elevated gas prices and a cyclospora outbreak that dented volumes.

item.title: Trump administration sued over fatal Minneapolis shooting
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: The family of Renee Good, one of two U.S. citizens fatally shot by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, sued the Trump administration on Thursday, saying there had been “no accountability” for her killing during deportation sweeps.

item.title: Paramount names Mattel boss Kreiz as co-CEO
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Paramount Skydance named Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz, who led the toymaker’s transformation into a broader entertainment company, as the co-CEO of the combined firm following its $110 billion Warner Bros deal.

item.title: FDA advisers recommend flu vaccine strains
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: A panel of advisers to the US FDA on Thursday recommended the virus strains vaccine manufacturers should include for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza season.

item.title: Boeing workers approve latest contract offer, averting strike fears
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Boeing’s largest white-collar union said on Thursday its members approved a sweetened contract offer, easing fears of a strike that could have stalled work on two long-delayed jetliners and slowed the pace of aircraft deliveries.

item.title: Trump’s threat to ban diesel exports sets off global alarms
item.dc:creator: New York Times
item.description: LONDON >> The Iran war has sent diesel prices soaring around the world, straining national budgets, adding costs to businesses and snarling supply chains from farms to ports.

item.title: Mortgage rates keep climbing, leading some buyers to riskier loans
item.dc:creator: New York Times
item.description: Mortgage rates continue to creep higher, compounding an affordability crunch that has squeezed many Americans’ wallets. Now soaring rates are prompting some homebuyers to roll the dice that they will fall in a few years.

item.title: Tropical Storm Nolo threatens Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument
item.dc:creator: Star-Advertiser Staff
item.description: UPDATE: 5 p.m.

item.title: Tennessee inmate gets ‘life-saving medical care’ after surviving botched execution
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Christa Pike was critically ill and receiving “life-saving medical care” in a Nashville hospital today hours after she survived two attempts by Tennessee to execute her with lethal injections, her lawyers said, renewing scrutiny of capital punishment in the United States.

item.title: Former Hawaii QB Luke Weaver leads San Jose State’s offense
item.dc:creator: Stephen Tsai
item.description: For quarterback Luke Weaver, Hawaii was a football paradise.

item.title: Former Hawaii congresswoman Pat Saiki remembered as political trailblazer
item.dc:creator: Andrew Gomes
item.description: One of Hawaii’s most accomplished Republican political leaders, Pat Saiki, whose service in Congress and the state Legislature spanned four decades, died Wednesday in Honolulu.

item.title: Curry praises the late Don Nelson, his first coach with the Warriors
item.dc:creator: Kyle Sakamoto
item.description: The Golden State Warriors’ Steph Curry recently signed a contract that will keep him with the franchise for his 18th and 19th seasons.

item.title: Coach Lue looking for Clippers to be consistently tough-minded
item.dc:creator: Billy Hull
item.description: As much as Tyronn Lue tries to maintain a positive outlook during training camp this week in Hawaii, the task that lies ahead looks incredibly grim.

item.title: Prep football preview: OIA playoff puzzle taking shape in D-I
item.dc:creator: Paul Honda
item.description: The puzzle is being solved one piece at a time. Or, maybe, several questions will be answered this weekend as the pieces for playoff spots fall into place.

item.title: HPU women’s volleyball falls to Jessup
item.dc:creator: Kyle Sakamoto
item.description: Mia Rivera finished with 16 kills and Jenna Kraft added 11 as the Jessup women’s volleyball team defeated Hawaii Pacific 25-23, 21-25, 25-20, 25-22 on Wednesday at St. Francis’ Shark Tank.

item.title: No. 4 Kahuku sweeps Roosevelt, earns bye in OIA playoffs
item.dc:creator: Paul Honda
item.description: Talia Soliai-Tui and Haley Kotobalavu had eight kills each as the No. 4-ranked Kahuku volleyball team swept Roosevelt 25-12, 25-23, 25-19 on Wednesday night at the Rough Riders’ shiny new gym.

item.title: Editorial cartoon for Thursday, October 1, 2026
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: By Derek Kalani and Chelsee Yee

item.title: Letter: Stop AI before doomsday scenario becomes reality
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: I’m on the threshold of 90 years on our planet and I now see another potential doomsday scenario. In a recent Star-Advertiser edition, it was reported that the U.S. has announced it has deployed weapons that can be launched from space (“U.S. deploys weapons in space to contend with Russia, China,” Sept. 16).

item.title: Shorter stays, storms curb Hawaii tourism
item.dc:creator: Allison Schaefers
item.description: Hawaii’s visitor industry lost momentum in August as fewer travelers came to the islands, stayed for shorter vacations and spent less overall amid storms and hurricane threats that disrupted what is typically one of the summer’s busiest tourism months.

item.title: Letter: Big AI firms using politics to create monopolies
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: Parlaying the trillion-dollar AI initial public offering with an election’s continuous fearmongering tactics should be illegal. There are a few huge, rich companies dominating the new AI revolution who want all other upcoming companies to slow down. The big firms want to set the rules and take control of establishing government regulations.

item.title: Letter: Extra fee for credit card transactions unjustified
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: In a recent Kokua Line, a reader complained about the city adding a service charge when using a payment method other than cash or check (“Readers question fees to use debit cards,” Aug. 30).

item.title: Letter: HMSA-HPH tie-up should expand disaster services
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: The proposed collaboration or merger between Hawaii Pacific Health and HMSA is often viewed and evaluated in terms of impacts on consumers, physicians and finances. However, with the increase in natural disasters hitting Hawaii, criteria relating to services to the most vulnerable during storms should be added.

item.title: Letter: Ads mislead voters on RISE bond benefits
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: The commercials tug at your heart. It says that voting “yes” on constitutional amendment 2 will fix potholes, bridges and aging infrastructure. Hawaii News Now’s Daryl Huff has a story detailing what ConAm 2 is all about. It is basically for developers to use RISE (“Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity”) bonds to fund new infrastructure development. Money will supposedly be recouped by higher property taxes in the new development.

item.title: Ex-Moanalua coach facing child porn charge accused of exploiting girl
item.dc:creator: Peter Boylan
item.description: A former Moanalua High School girls wrestling coach facing federal criminal charges for sexually exploiting an underage girl was reported to the Honolulu Police Department in 2012 after he allegedly kissed a 13-year-old Roosevelt High School student.

item.title: Mayor seeks Charter status for Honolulu culture and arts office
item.dc:creator: Ian Bauer
item.description: Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi is asking the City Council to formally establish the Mayor’s Office of Culture and the Arts in the City Charter, a move the administration says would give the 55-year-old program greater authority and stability across future city administrations.

item.title: Hawaii County looks to dismiss case of teen killed after being hit by officer’s car
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: A Hawaii County attorney argued Tuesday in court that a Hawaii Police Department officer who hit and killed a pedestrian with a police car nearly three years ago is immune from liability, but an attorney for the family of the victim, a 16-year-old boy, argued the officer was negligent and liable.

item.title: Kokua Line: When will problem with Hawaii’s REAL ID clear up?
item.dc:creator: Christine Donnelly
item.description: Question: When will the problem with the new driver’s licenses be cleared up? When did they know about this? I have an appointment to renew my license in a few weeks.

item.title: Japan’s population includes more than 100,000 people age 100 or older
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: There are now more than 100,000 centenarians in Japan, a record for a country famous for its longevity.

item.title: Off the news: Plug in on Hawaian Electric’s rate hikes
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: It’s the public’s turn to chime in on Hawaiian Electric’s bid to raise base rates, which the utility contends is necessary to combat inflation, pay for increased insurance premiums and compensate for aging fossil fuel-burning generators.

item.title: Column: Local architecture is much more than beautiful buildings
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: Every October, architects and design communities around the world celebrate Architecture Month, or “Archtober.” This year, it arrives alongside World Habitat Day on Oct. 5, a United Nations observance that asks us to consider the places where we live and our shared responsibility for the future of our communities.

item.title: Editorial: Take steps to clear Kaimuki eatery
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: It’s good to see that a surge of community stink — aka complaints — has prodded city and state officials into action to prevent a larger, literal stink that had been festering in Kaimuki.

item.title: Off the news: City breaks ground on Kahuku EMS facility
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: Work has finally begun on a long-awaited new Emergency Medical Services headquarters in Kahuku. When completed in December 2028, the North Shore station will be more than 3,000 square feet, thrice the size of the current 900 square foot facility built in 1997.
